citations.description: File reviewed in full; no MCP tool call test found.

findings.criterion: A test asserts an MCP tool returns an error payload (not a dead server) with REBAR_ROOT unset in a non-repo cwd
findings.detail: No test was found that directly invokes an MCP tool (e.g., via build_server().call_tool(...) or equivalent in-memory MCP client) with REBAR_ROOT unset in a non-repo cwd and asserts that an error payload is returned rather than the server dying. The evidence confirms only library-level tests (asserting TrackerRootError is raised), a CLI boundary test, and a static AST scan of MCP source files. These provide indirect assurance but do not satisfy the criterion, which explicitly requires a test that drives an actual MCP tool call and asserts an error payload response.
findings.remediation: Add a test that uses an in-memory MCP client (e.g., build_server().call_tool(...)) with REBAR_ROOT unset and a non-repo working directory, and asserts the tool returns an error payload rather than crashing the server.
findings.title: Missing MCP tool error-payload test

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: use the evidence path that matches each one. For codebase-verifiable work, complete any unfinished work and make its proof discoverable in the repository. For evidence that inherently lives outside the repository, mark the criterion with the exact `[operator-attested]` tag and add a comment to this ticket that documents the concrete artifacts that meet it (commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the evidence to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so properly tagged evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. An untagged external criterion cannot be satisfied by a ticket comment alone. Then re-verify.
